context: Marks of students in an exam, grouped in sets of equal width.
stem: The frequency distribution shows the marks of {=n} students in an exam. Sets (marks): {=s0}–{=s0+w}, {=s0+w}–{=s0+2*w}, {=s0+2*w}–{=s0+3*w}, {=s0+3*w}–{=s0+4*w}, {=s0+4*w}–{=s0+5*w} with frequencies {=a}, {=b}, {=c}, {=b}, {=a} respectively. Using the centres of the sets, find the standard deviation of the marks.
solution: $\sum k = {=n}$ and, by symmetry of the frequencies, the mean $\bar{x}$ equals the middle centre {=mu}.
notes: Frequencies (a,b,6a,b,a) make variance = w^2 exactly; sigma = w. Centres are integers since w even.
